title: D–A–M Bottleneck Diagnostic
briefing: Use the official chapter and Lab 01 collection to diagnose a degraded model before spending on a solution.
objectives: Classify evidence along the data, algorithm, and machine axes.
Reject a solution that does not target the observed bottleneck.
Connect a technical metric to the mission outcome.

prediction.prompt: Accuracy drops while code and serving latency remain stable; training data is eighteen months old. Which first action is best?

options.label: Audit data freshness and population shift

steps.title: Inventory evidence
steps.instructions: List the observed model, data, machine, and mission signals without adding facts that the scenario did not provide.

steps.title: Rank hypotheses
steps.instructions: Propose one hypothesis per D–A–M axis and name the cheapest measurement that could reject each hypothesis.

steps.title: Make the decision
steps.instructions: Choose the first experiment, estimate its cost and information value, and define the result that would change your plan.

evidenceChecklist.label: All three D–A–M axes are considered
The next action has an explicit decision rule

reflectionPrompts: Why is adding compute attractive even when it does not target the bottleneck?
What production signal would detect this failure sooner?
extensionChallenge: Repeat the diagnosis for a system whose accuracy is stable but p99 latency violates its service objective on a mobile target.
